messages:
Kayla_support: Incoming support case — customer says their free-trial was blocked by fraud checks. They claim they're a small YC startup and used promo STARTUP2026 but it didn't apply. Email used: devteam@mailinator.com, signup IP: 18.47.99.21 (likely VPN), user agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh). Account id: acct_0xA12B. Customer asks for a manual trial grant so they can run a quick POC. Any quick guidance?

fraud-bot: ALERT: acct_0xA12B triggered rules: disposable_email, vpn_ip, promo_mismatch. Fraud score: 82. See https://internal.redwood/fraud/0xA12B 

Matt_fraud: Can you paste the raw signup headers + timestamp and any other accounts from the same IP? Also did the promo code succeed server-side or was it rejected?

Kayla_support: Pasting what I have from the support ticket and signup logs:
```
signup_ts: 2026-02-14T21:03:12Z
email: devteam@mailinator.com
ip: 18.47.99.21
user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7)
promo_attempt: STARTUP2026 -> code_status: rejected (reason: promo_not_eligible)
notes: promo applied in UI but server returned 403 promo_ineligible
```

Kayla_support: Quick repro steps I ran locally: created a throwaway account with mailinator + ran the same promo -> backend returned promo_ineligible and account got auto-flagged by rules engine. Screenshot link: https://assets.redwood/support/attachments/1801234567/ss.png

Sana_billing: Policy check — we do allow manual grants in edge cases (verified startups / sales leads) but require some verification. We can issue a one-time manual trial credit (default 100 credits / 24h) but we need either a corporate domain or a short KYC (incorporation link or public repo). Since email is disposable and IP flagged as VPN, we should ask for a corporate email first. If they can provide a github/org link or a domain, we can grant.

Matt_fraud: Quick look through logs: same IP (18.47.99.21) created 3 accounts in last 36h, all using mailinator variants. Promo STARTUP2026 was used twice on two accounts; both were rejected. No payment instrument on file. Given score 82 and repeated disposable emails, I recommend deny automatic grant but allow manual if customer provides corporate proof. If they insist, we can grant temporarily but tag as "monitor/high-risk" and set a 24h grace.

Kayla_support: Customer replied: "we're legit — here's our repo https://github.com/petitstartup/ai-proj and website https://petitstartup.com (domain registered 2024). We can provide a company email if needed." They asked if you can expedite — they're blocked from a demo tomorrow.

Sana_billing: Ok, that repo + domain looks reasonable. Manual path: grant 100 credits, note account as manual-trial-grant, require corporate email verification within 7 days. If no verification, revoke credits and close account. Kayla, please issue the grant and add the note.

Kayla_support: Done — granted promo code TRIAL-MANUAL-24H (100 credits), expiry: 2026-02-15T21:03:12Z. Account tag: manual_trial_granted; fraud note added: "repo+domain provided; 24h manual grant; require corporate email within 7 days". I messaged the customer with steps and asked for a company email or incorporation doc. :white_check_mark:

Matt_fraud: Thanks. I'll set a watch on acct_0xA12B for anomalous usage and duplicate IP signups. If we see the mailinator pattern continue, we escalate to blocklist.

Sana_billing: Thanks team — please keep the ticket open until we either verify or revoke. Kayla, please escalate back to me if the customer pushes for long-term credits without verification.

Kayla_support: Will do. Leaving thread open. Customer notified and next step is corporate email or docs. :slightly_smiling_face:
